and it fails interaction necessity, which disregards event times. Interaction-sensitive selection under
the reciprocal potential therefore requires receiver-dependent targets, such as selective channels
with nonconstant Gibbs rows.

6.10 The formation standard

The thesis of the theory is that interactions between agents can produce further agents. A definition
of formation must therefore exclude three ways in which the selection and inheritance clauses can
be met without any such production. A parent that retains every child state compresses nothing:
four agents with laws N (xi, 1) under symmetric peer-KL consensus, a threshold selector, and
the identity retention select two pairs and then their union with exact inheritance at every stage.
Agents that do not interact can be grouped by any rule that reads their initial data and a common
relaxation clock. A second stage that forms from every handoff whatever the first stage produced is
a sequence of supplied scales rather than recursion. The standard below makes each exclusion a
clause.

                                                            72
6. Inherited Parents and Recursive Formation      MAgent Theory 2.0

Definition 6.30 (Null flow). Let a construction specify a flow  generated by a potential of the
form eq. (4.4) or by the per-agent dynamics of definition 4.19, together with references, evaluators,
source priors, temperatures, a selector, and an admitted class of initial configurations. Its null
flow 0 is the flow obtained by deleting every peer cost Diqj, Disj with j = i and evaluating every
law-dependent channel and evaluator at its value with the peer laws held at their initial values,
with all other data unchanged. The membership history H(x) of an initial configuration x is the
sequence of selected partitions with their event times; H0(x) is the history produced by the same
selector along 0. The partition sequence P (x) is H(x) with its event times removed, and P 0(x) is
obtained from H0(x) in the same way.

Definition 6.31 (Inherited recursive formation). An inherited recursive formation is a construction
satisfying all of the following clauses.

(F1) Admitted class. The initial configurations form a nonempty set that is open in a declared
       topology on a declared space of initially unpartitioned configurations, or a declared invariant
       family.

(F2) Selection. The dynamics selects nontrivial blocks with a declared persistence criterion, and
       each handoff is a measurable function of the state or of accessible history.

(F3) Inheritance. Each selected block carries inherited belief and model laws, evaluators, boundary
       responses, and dynamics in the sense of this chapter, with the class of admitted probes fixed
       before the retention is chosen.

(F4) Compression. Each handoff retention is non-injective on the post-handoff invariant set, and
       some admitted child-level probe distinguishes two configurations with the same retained
       value.

(F5) Interaction necessity. P = P 0 on a nonempty open subset of the admitted class. A difference
       only in event times does not count.

(F6) Recursion. The parents select a block containing at least two first-stage parents under the
       inherited interactions, without resetting their source data or supplying a newly tuned attraction,
       and this second-stage selection does not occur from every counterfactual handoff in the
       inherited class.

A construction satisfies the strong form of (F5) if its final partition is not a function of any statistic of
the initial data whose evolution is the same under  and 0. It is amplifying if, at each event, the
ratio of the largest within-block diameter to the smallest between-block distance is smaller along 
than along 0 by a declared factor below one. Write (F6a) for the first sentence of (F6), a second
selection among first-stage parents under the inherited interactions without reset or retuning, and
(F6b) for its counterfactual part. A construction satisfying (F1), (F2), (F3), and (F6a) but failing at
least one of (F4), (F5), and (F6b) is a two-stage selection with exact inheritance; a construction with
only one selection stage that satisfies (F1) to (F3) is a single-stage selection with exact inheritance.
The clauses that fail are always stated.

Persistence can mean an invariant block relation in deterministic dynamics or a specified path event
in stochastic dynamics. Clause (F5) is a control experiment: it asks whether the grouping would
occur with the interaction switched off. Clause (F4) excludes the identity retention described above,
and (F6) is the counterfactual-handoff requirement. The finite construction of this chapter settles

                                              73
6. Inherited Parents and Recursive Formation      MAgent Theory 2.0

inheritance for a supplied hierarchy and makes no selection claim. Chapter 7 gives a construction
with explicit fusion events under a nonsmooth interaction; at zero coupling its agents never collide,
so it meets (F5), but fused children are identical, so it fails (F4), and it fails (F6b); it is a two-stage
selection with exact inheritance. The erasure construction of chapter 9 is a single-stage selection
with exact inheritance. Under the original smooth potential, chapter 12 selects two parents and then
their union on a prepared common-precision family, but its membership schedule is independent of
the coupling (proposition 12.7), so it fails (F5); since the union also forms from every counterfactual
handoff with sufficiently separated parents, it fails (F6b) as well, and it is a two-stage selection
with exact inheritance. Chapter 13 gives a six-agent construction on a full open law neighborhood
with native preferential selection; it meets (F4) and (F6a), but in the regime of its proof the null
flow reproduces its membership history, so its theorem does not establish (F5), and (F6b) is not
verified; it is a two-stage selection with exact inheritance. Both smooth constructions supply their
compression architectures.

Open problem 6.32 (A recursive formation). The normalized per-agent construction of chapter 14
supplies a complementary one-stage result. It proves persistent interaction-dependent grouping
with conflicting records and a physically noninjective parent preserving its declared port dynamics,
finite adaptive histories, and nonflat geometry on a finite window. The sufficient phase interface is
predeclared and the parent retains primitive ports. Joining already canonical parents loses no new
coordinate, so neither a second compressive handoff nor (F6b) follows.

Construct a population dynamics under the reciprocal potential, the per-agent free energies, or a
global free energy that satisfies (F1) to (F6), preferably in the strong and amplifying forms, and
derive rather than declare its selector and its compression interface.

                                              74
Chapter 7

Finite Fusion with Exact Statistical
Inheritance

This chapter constructs a population whose dynamics makes agents coincide at finite times and
whose coincident blocks carry exact inherited laws, evaluator, metric, and responses. The dynamics
is a nonsmooth modification of the reciprocal law potential of definition 4.2: each peer divergence
is replaced by the square root of twice that divergence, source rows are fixed, and the laws are
restricted to a lognormal family with fixed variances. It is not a free energy of any normalized model,
and its conclusions do not transfer to the smooth potential or to the per-agent and global free
energies of chapter 4.

Pairwise fusion penalties occur in convex clustering [77], and suitable nonsmooth consensus
protocols produce finite-time agreement [33]. On the restricted family the square-root interaction is
exactly the absolute-value kernel, so in each sector the population is a weighted particle solution
of the one-dimensional aggregation equation with attractive kernel |x|, whose sticky collisions
and finite-time total collapse are known [19, 26]. What the construction adds is the inheritance
bookkeeping: represented laws, model evaluator, transport, parent metric, and boundary kernels
descend exactly through each collision. Its dynamical outcome is a finite coalescence tree that
ends in global consensus for every initial datum (proposition 7.3); persistent heterogeneous
organization does not occur. Section 7.7 reports the construction against the formation standard of
definition 6.31.

Remark 7.10 (Sufficiency beyond the lognormal family). The kernel eq. (7.39) is the conditional
law of the children given their sufficient statistic, and it is free of the parameter for that reason. The
same holds for any family with a sufficient statistic for independent children: the parent law is the
law of the statistic, the Fisher metric of the children restricted to equal parameters is multiplied
by the multiplicity, and the parameter-free conditional law supplies both the message kernel and
the joint reconstruction. For Gamma children of shape k, for example, one child given the sum S
of n children is S times a Beta(k, (n - 1)k) variable. The ingredient specific to Gaussian location
families is that the square-root divergence between restored messages is the convex function |µ|;
on a general regular family it equals the Fisher distance only to leading order near the diagonal,
and global uniqueness would need semiconvexity estimates in place of convexity.

Parameter retention has a narrower meaning. On an exactly synchronized stratum, child means
are redundant copies; retaining their common value does not identify different nonsynchronized
configurations. Away from that stratum, a block average need not determine its external sign forces.
Equation (7.36) makes no claim about such hidden parameter fibers.

The admitted boundary protocol draws fresh messages through Bn, fresh predictive messages
through eq. (7.11), or complete fresh represented samples through the joint reconstruction. To type
an accessible stored readout, augment the complete population configuration by o  O = (0, )
and set (µ, n, o) = o. At declared epochs, the transition  advances the deterministic parameter
flow and overwrites o using the selected normalized scalar output kernel. Between epochs, o is
fixed, and it never enters the mean equation. Retention copies this accessible o exactly; it does not
claim access to cached private residual samples. For vector readouts the same definition uses the
corresponding finite product space and joint kernel. Equal parameter trajectories and conditional
output kernels imply equal joint accessible readout laws for every finite sequence of such queries,
by multiplying successive conditional kernels. Reusing persistent latent samples or introducing
record feedback requires another state specification.

7.7 Status against the formation standard

We now check the clauses of definition 6.31. The admitted class of eq. (7.32), with all label
permutations, is open in the declared invariant common-offset family, and by corollary 7.7 the
same history holds on an open subset of the full space, so (F1) holds. Blocks are selected by
attained equality in both sectors, they persist by lemma 7.2, and the handoff is the partition of the
current state into coincident agents, so (F2) holds. Laws, evaluator, metric, rows, contacts, and the
declared fresh-message, predictive, reconstruction, and stored-readout responses are inherited
exactly on synchronized strata, with the probe class fixed before the retention, so (F3) holds.

The null flow of definition 6.30 deletes the pair terms, which is the case  = 0. Each agent then
follows the linear equation µ i = -Aµi, whose flow is invertible, so distinct agents never coincide
and H0 contains no event. By proposition 7.3, every configuration with two distinct agents has at

                                                     84
7. Finite Fusion with Exact Statistical Inheritance      MAgent Theory 2.0

least one event along . Hence H = H0 on the whole admitted class, and (F5) holds. The strong
form of (F5) fails trivially, because the final partition is the single block for every initial datum. The
construction is amplifying only in the degenerate sense that within-block diameters vanish at each
event.

Clause (F4) fails. On the post-handoff invariant set the children of a block are identical copies, so
the retention of common means and multiplicity is injective there; child frames are fixed passive
data that no admitted probe reads in reference coordinates. The geometric mean is noninjective on
sample vectors, but samples are not configurations, and the conditional law of the child samples
given the retained sample is the parameter-free kernel eq. (7.39), so no admitted child-level probe
distinguishes two configurations with the same retained value. Clause (F6a) holds: by theorem 7.6
and corollary 7.7, the two first-stage parents select their union under the inherited interaction, with
no reset of their data and no retuned coupling. Clause (F6b) fails. By proposition 7.3 applied to
multiplicities two, every configuration of two first-stage parents, whatever their means, fuses at a
finite time, so the second-stage selection occurs from every counterfactual handoff in the inherited
class; the order of the stages is the order of the initial gaps fixed by eq. (7.32).

The construction is therefore not a recursive formation. It satisfies (F1), (F2), (F3), (F5), and (F6a)
and fails (F4) and (F6b), so it is a two-stage selection with exact inheritance: a finite coalescence in
which the interaction is necessary for the grouping, the grouping is a coalescence tree ordered by
the initial gaps, and the tree always ends in one block.

Remark 7.11 (Smooth peer KL dynamics and persistent parents). The finite mergers above
depend on the nonsmooth interaction. Under the smooth reciprocal potential with a locally Lipschitz
vector field, an interior trajectory cannot first reach an invariant synchronization manifold at finite
time (proposition 6.22), so smooth constructions need a different selection criterion; the threshold
selectors of chapters 12 and 13 are such criteria, and the remaining problem is open problem 6.32.
Persistent parents are excluded here by proposition 7.3. A contact range, for example ij =
1{|µi - µj| < } as in bounded-confidence dynamics [74], or a multiwell local reference would
let separated blocks stop interacting. Both destroy the convexity on which uniqueness rests, and
well-posedness and inheritance for such variants have not been established.

Chapter 8

Sufficient States for Smooth KL
Evolution

This chapter works with the reciprocal law potential of definition 4.2 and its unit-mobility Fisher flow;
its conclusions concern that potential, not the per-agent or global free energies of chapter 4. The
question is which information a coarse description of an agent must keep when an exact reduction
is wanted while agents remain different. We first identify the conditional information that enters a
retained force, then construct an exact state completion made of general probability laws for one
architecture: fixed independent private reference factors, and receiver reconstruction channels that
discard the sender's private coordinate. These channels are additional constitutive data within the
potential, not a consequence of an arbitrary law-dependent transport.

In this architecture the private sector is passive. Each private conditional relaxes along an explicit
exponential arc toward its reference, independently of every public law, row, and other agent, and it
acts on the public flow only as open-loop forcing through its conditional KL profile. The completion
is therefore a solvable baseline. Its compression is the equimeasurability quotient of each private
log density under its declared reference: it forgets which private point carries a log-density value,
so it identifies distinct conditionals only when the reference has nontrivial symmetry, and it is not
minimal for the public flow (proposition 8.10). It fails once a channel transmits the sender's private
data (remark 8.12). The construction selects no group of agents, so the interaction-necessity clause
of definition 6.31 does not apply to it; its private sector evolves identically under the null flow of
definition 6.30, because the conditional equations contain no peer term.

8.1 The force that survives marginalization

Let Q be a positive law on a standard Borel space, let C be a measurable statistic, and write
µ = C#Q. Suppose a differentiable functional has variational derivative hQ and Fisher velocity

Q = -Q(hQ - EQhQ).                           (8.1)

All identities below are immediate for finite positive tables. On general spaces they need a
dominated differentiable path, square-integrable scores, and integrability that permits the displayed
conditional expectations and differentiations. Statements about flows on general spaces are made
under the hypotheses of hypothesis 8.4, which give unique solutions in bounded log-density charts
(proposition 8.8); they do not assert existence on every space of probability measures.

Proposition 8.1 (Conditional mean force). The retained velocity is

µ = -µ (EQ[hQ | C] - EQhQ) .                 (8.2)

86
8. Sufficient States for Smooth KL Evolution                             MAgent Theory 2.0

Consequently, an autonomous velocity for µ exists on an admitted class precisely when the centered
conditional mean on the right is determined by µ on that class. If, in addition, the admitted class is
invariant under the fine flow and the resulting retained equation µ = V (µ) has unique solutions,
then two fine trajectories in the class with the same initial marginal have the same marginal at all
common times.

Proof. For every bounded measurable f , integrate f (C) against eq. (8.1) and condition on C.
This gives the weak form of eq. (8.2). Two laws with the same marginal have the same marginal
velocity if and only if their centered conditional forces agree almost everywhere under that marginal.
Invariance keeps both fine trajectories in the class, so each marginal solves µ = V (µ), and
uniqueness identifies them.

Equation eq. (8.2) is the class-mean aggregation of a replicator equation over types, familiar
from the Price equation of selection [122]. For Q(dz, dv) = µ(dz)z(dv) and a fixed reference
P (dz, dv) = (dz)z(dv), the local KL force illustrates the missing information:

                                  dµ              H(z) = DKL(zz).        (8.3)
EQ[log(dQ/dP ) | z] = log d (z) + H(z),

Thus a scalar total conditional loss does not usually determine the retained force. Its dependence
on z matters. The Fisher metric makes the same separation: if a score is f (z, v) = f1(z) + f2(z, v),
with Eµf1 = 0 and Ez f2 = 0, then

gQ(f Q, f Q) = f1(z)2µ(dz) +                      f2(z, v)2z(dv) µ(dz).  (8.4)

The cross term vanishes by conditional centering. This calculation is consistent with the statistical
behavior of Fisher information under sufficient statistics [5]. Dynamical sufficiency asks a different
question: it preserves the specified evolution and responses, and need not preserve inference
about every discarded parameter.

Corollary 8.2 (Pushforward as a Fisher submersion). On a regular positive class, the differential
of Q  C#Q sends the tangent f Q to EQ[f | C]µ. Its kernel consists of the scores with zero
conditional mean given C, and it is isometric on scores that are functions of C. If the functional has
the form E = Ec  C#, the retained marginal follows the Fisher gradient flow of Ec at the same time.

Proof. For bounded g, g(C)f dQ = g EQ[f | C] dµ, which identifies the pushforward tangent.
With f1 = EQ[f | C] and f2 = f - f1, eq. (8.4) gives the kernel and the isometry. If E = Ec  C#, the
chain rule gives hQ = hc  C up to a constant, so eq. (8.2) becomes µ = -µ(hc - Eµhc).

This is the equality case of the monotonicity of Fisher information under statistics [6]; the content of
the present chapter is the case in which hQ is not a function of C.

8.3 An exact law-valued completion

Definition 8.6 (Conditional log-density spectrum). For a private reference A and conditional

density z, define

                       z = (z)#A, z = log(dz/dA).                    (8.12)

This probability law records how much reference mass carries each log-density value. It forgets
which private point carries that value. It obeys

                       erz(dr) = 1, H(z) = rerz(dr).                 (8.13)

The spectrum is the law under A of the log-likelihood ratio of the dichotomy (z, A). For mutually
absolutely continuous pairs, equal spectra are equivalent to Blackwell equivalence of the two
dichotomies [17, 138]. Two conditionals have the same spectrum exactly when their log densities
are equimeasurable under A. The compression is therefore a property of the declared reference,
not of the dynamics. On a finite private alphabet z({r}) = A({z = r}), so if no two distinct sets of
atoms of A have equal mass, equal spectra force equal level sets and hence equal conditionals:
the retention is injective. With A = (0.6, 0.4), for example, the conditionals (3/4, 1/4) and (1/4, 3/4)
have the different spectra with atoms log(5/4), log(5/8) and log(5/12), log(15/8) at masses 0.6, 0.4.
Noninjectivity requires a reference with equal-mass sets of atoms, such as a uniform finite reference,
or an atomless reference. The log-Laplace transform of the spectrum is

                   z(b) = log ebrz(dr) = (b - 1)Db(zA),              (8.14)

where Db is the Rényi divergence of order b [139]. Under (H1) the spectrum has compact support,
so z on (0, 1] determines z.

This is a configuration retention. Its spectra can be infinite-dimensional, and there is no claim that

with Q0, whereas the retained conditional erzt (dr) is supported on a supp z0 - log Zz(a), which
moves unless z = A. The spectral evolution is a continuity equation in r with velocity H(z) - r.

Remark 8.12 (Which channels permit the completion). Receiver reconstruction is not what
produces closure. If every channel in a row is replaced by Biqj(zj, dzi)Aqi (dvi), a fixed reconstruction
independent of state and source, the chain rule gives Diqj = DKL(µiµjBiqj) + Hiqdµi. The added

the private energy doubles, and the conditional equation becomes tqi,z = 2(Hiq(z) - qi,z); the
spectrum still closes. What matters is that the channel discards the sender's private coordinate.

A channel that transmits it fails. Take a trivial public space, V = {1, 2} with uniform A, two agents

attending to each other through the identity channel, and 1 = (3/4, 1/4). With 2 = 1 the peer

costs  vanish,  whereas  with  2  =  (1/4, 3/4),  which  has  the  same  spectrum,  each  peer  cost  is  1  log 3

and the peer forces move 1 toward 2. The spectral velocity of agent 1 then differs between two

configurations with the same per-agent spectra, so those spectra are not a closed state. For identity

private channels on a common (V, A), every peer integrand is a function of the vector (k(v))k at
one private point, which suggests the joint law of that vector under A as the retained state; its

closure and its compression are not established here.

8.4 Boundary records and feedback

Public-only response kernels descend immediately: the channels Biqj, Bisj and evaluator Gic are
determined by the retained public laws. A private-sensitive response needs more information.
In eq. (8.19), let the probabilities of record 1 at the two private points be (3/4, 1/4). The two
conditionals yield record probabilities 5/8 and 3/8. After record 1, their private posteriors are
(9/10, 1/10) and (1/2, 1/2). Thus an unmarked spectrum can fail both the boundary test and the
next-update test.

There is an exact completion for a specified family of records. Fix a measurable mark T : V  D,
with D standard Borel, through which every allowed private readout factors. Retain

                                              z = (z, T )#A.                                              (8.22)

8. Sufficient States for Smooth KL Evolution                MAgent Theory 2.0

The correlation between the log-density value and the mark is retained. For a normalized record
kernel with strictly positive density L(o | z, d), assume the following integrals are finite and nonzero
and each updated law stays in the admitted regular domain. A bounded log likelihood is a sufficient
local condition for the conditional log-density bounds. Put

Between records, eqs. (8.15) and (8.16) transport the first coordinate of z and leave its mark fixed.

Proof. Since dz = ez dA, integration of the likelihood gives eq. (8.23). Bayes' rule gives the
displayed marginal update and dz+/dA = ez L(o | z, T )/Nz(o). Taking the logarithm and pushing

update is therefore the same equation with this new conditional law. Inductively, the inherited flow
gives the next retained state, the inherited record kernel gives the same next-record law, and the
inherited update gives the same posterior retained state. Actions selected from retained histories
preserve this induction. Any reference or likelihood parameters changed by records must also be
retained and updated by a rule that depends only on this state.

The composite of flow intervals and these updates is the record-interrupted dynamics of defini-
tion 4.24. The potential contains no record term and is not monotone across records. Records act
only at their times: no rule changing the references is declared here, and between records each
conditional relaxes toward its fixed reference by eq. (8.18), so the effect of a record on the private
sector decays.

The update is sectorwise. A product of separate belief and model likelihoods preserves the recogni-
tion restriction qi  si. A likelihood jointly coupling the two sectors need not preserve that product;
exact joint conditioning would require a joint recognition state, or a separately declared projection.
Marked feedback can also destroy equality of unmarked spectra across public coordinates. The
augmented marked state still closes, but the simpler conclusion of corollary 8.9 then need not hold.

For an explicit retained sample law, use

Qc(dz, dr, dd) = µ(dz)erz(dr, dd).                          (8.25)

8. Sufficient States for Smooth KL Evolution                       MAgent Theory 2.0

It is normalized and reproduces every declared marked record. It is the pushforward under the
current, law-dependent statistic (z, v)  (z, z(v), T (v)). Different assignments of density values to
private points within a mark can give the same retained state. If the permitted records distinguish
every private point, the mark may have to retain that point, eliminating this compression. The
boundary protocol therefore fixes what can be forgotten. Predictive-state constructions likewise
make sufficiency relative to future observations [130]; the formulas here specify the state and
update for this particular KL architecture.

8.5 What is still required for formation

Positive source temperature does not give exact isolation by itself. For optimized rows, every
allowed finite-cost edge has positive weight. For a dynamic row, set

                                              jk  =  log  j /j  .  (8.26)
                                                          k /k

The Fisher row equation from eq. (4.4) gives

jk = -(Dj - Dk) - Tqjk.                                            (8.27)

Multiplying by eTqt and integrating shows that finite cost differences keep every such ratio finite on a
regular finite interval. Initially positive weights therefore stay positive there. Uniformly bounded cost
differences also bound these ratios for all time and prevent asymptotic disappearance of an allowed
weight. A formed collective may nevertheless keep nonzero boundary interactions; isolation is not
required for inheritance.

The construction above compresses private conditional information of each agent separately, and
only up to the equimeasurability quotient of its declared reference. It does not combine several
distinct public agent laws into one smaller collective state. Retaining their complete labeled tuple
and calling it a parent would leave that aggregation problem untouched; whether a retention of
such a tuple compresses is decided by clause (F4) of definition 6.31, which requires a noninjective
retention whose fibers some admitted child-level probe distinguishes. Nor does recognizing a
persistent source-preference group establish a compatible collective retention. The distinction
between a coarse observable and an autonomous macroscopic evolution is also expressed by flow
intertwining in Barnett and Seth [9].

Remark 8.14 (Aggregation with conditional information retained). The construction of this
chapter selects no group and involves no grouping of agents, and its private sector is unchanged
by deleting every peer cost. A recursive formation that uses the conditional-spectrum state as part
of its retention is an instance of open problem 6.32. A coupled architecture under the reciprocal
potential in which private conditionals feed back into public interactions, for example through private-
transmitting channels or rows that read private data, and which still admits an exact compressing
completion, is not available.

Chapter 9

State-Controlled Erasure and Persistent

This chapter concerns the reciprocal law potential of definition 4.2, in its exact Gibbs-reduced form
eq. (4.6); nothing in it is a statement about the per-agent or global free-energy pictures. Inside
that potential there is a conditional first-stage construction. A prescribed channel can lose its
dependence on some internal laws when a dynamically evolving gate coordinate enters a flat part
of that channel. The preferred sources of the remaining agents can change, and the retained
dynamics can then become exactly autonomous. The mechanism is an engineered constitutive
choice, and both of its conclusions follow from a declared ordering of scales. It supplies neither
a general explanation of sufficient interfaces nor a second formation stage. Measured against
the formation standard definition 6.31, it is a single-stage selection with exact inheritance by a
decoupled-factor projection; section 9.5 records the clause-by-clause status and the null-flow
control. The general laws of the preceding chapters remain the framework; the existence example
below uses an explicitly invariant family of positive finite laws.

9.3 A change of preferred sources without synchronization

Theorem 9.2 (Changing and persistent source preferences). For sufficiently small  > 0, admit

with equality exactly at equilibria. The set Q is compact and forward invariant by theorem 9.2.
By the invariance principle [92], the -limit set of each trajectory is a nonempty connected set of
equilibria in Q.

At  = 0 the public field decouples into single-agent fields. In the positive box their zeros solve
atanh x = Jy and atanh y = Jx. With the increasing map g(t) = atanh(t)/J this reads x = g(y) and
y = g(x). If x > g(x), then y = g(x) < x and x = g(y) < g(x), a contradiction; the case x < g(x)
is symmetric. Hence atanh x = Jx, and since atanh(x)/x increases from one and J > 1, the only
solution in (0, 1) is x = 1/2. The Jacobian of (atanh x - Jy, atanh y - Jx) there has diagonal entries
4/3 and off-diagonal entries -J, and 16/9 - J2 > 0, so the zero is nondegenerate. The negative
box is the mirror image. Thus at  = 0 the field on Q has exactly one zero, and it is nondegenerate
and interior.

The peer cost D is a smooth function of (x, v, ) that vanishes to second order in , so all its
derivatives in (x, v) are O(2) on Q, and the derivatives of the Gibbs rows are O(2/T ). For fixed T
the public field therefore converges to the decoupled field in C1(Q) as   0. The decoupled field
is bounded away from zero on Q outside any neighborhood of its zero, and the implicit function
theorem gives a unique nondegenerate zero inside a small neighborhood. This proves uniqueness
and the limit (1/2, 1/2).

The post-closure public system has identical constitutive data for all agents and uniform nonself
priors, so it is equivariant under permutations of the agents. It is also equivariant under the
global reversal (x, y)  (-x, -y), since d0 is even, Jxy is invariant, and d(-x, -c) = d(x, c). The
transposition of two box-mates, and the composition of global reversal with the exchange of the two
boxes, map Q to itself and therefore fix the unique equilibrium. This gives equal box-mates and
opposite boxes.

Every -limit set is therefore this single equilibrium. It attracts every interior point of Q, so it is a
local minimum of Epub: a nondegenerate critical point of a gradient flow that is not a minimum has a
stable set of positive codimension. The linearized gradient flow at a nondegenerate minimum has
negative spectrum, which gives exponential convergence.

agents each box carries a single attracting equilibrium, and proposition 9.3 forces its members
together. If agent i instead carried its own coupling Ji = log 3 + i, the single-agent equilibria near

Proposition 9.4 (Exact parent evolution and public responses). The inherited parent equations

are  d

     dt f (v)I (dv) = f (v) · V [v; M]I (dv),                        (9.25)

for every continuously differentiable test function. Among curves of realizable finite-atom states,
that is, empirical measures of solutions of the public system, two curves with equal initial retained
measures coincide at all later times. The retained measures also determine every declared fresh
public response whose source selection depends only on public states, including joint responses
with a shared sampled child.

Proof. Differentiate the finite sum in eq. (9.24) using the exact public equations. This gives
eq. (9.25). Equal retained parent measures admit enumerations that differ only by within-pair
permutations. Uniqueness and permutation equivariance of the public system give identical evolved
measures, proving the uniqueness assertion among realizable curves. For a fresh response, select
the child or children using the declared normalized public kernel, then integrate their public sample
laws against the retained empirical measures. Both the selection probabilities and sample laws are
determined by the retained states. For shared-source outputs, use one shared draw rather than
multiplying separate marginals; the same calculation preserves their joint law.

The proposition does not assert uniqueness for eq. (9.25) among general measure-valued curves;
that would need a Lipschitz stability estimate for V in (v, M). A single I has no autonomous
dynamics, since V [v; M] depends on the counting measure of both pairs; only the pair of parents
is closed. The descent also holds for every partition of the four agents, so inheritance does not
distinguish the selected pairs.

The parent can carry belief and model marginals qI = bxI (d(x, y)) and sI = byI (d(x, y)), with
normalized public evaluator GJ . These two marginals alone are insufficient: I retains the paired
public roles and receiver-specific routing information. The inherited equations are eq. (9.25), not a
Fisher flow of the reciprocal potential for the two mixture marginals. The parent is therefore not an
agent of the children's type: no law pair with an evaluator and a reciprocal KL interaction carries its
dynamics, and the construction cannot be iterated as it stands. A recursion would need a retention
whose image is again a law pair with an inherited reciprocal interaction.

The compression here discards the private and gate laws, which no admitted response reads after
closure: the admitted family has twenty-four continuous means, and the retained empirical state

                     104
9. State-Controlled Erasure and Persistent Source Preferences  MAgent Theory 2.0

keeps eight public means, up to within-pair permutations. It is a decoupled-factor projection followed
by a finite label quotient, and it keeps every public child state. Cached private readouts, feedback
that changes the erased channels, and protocols that later inspect discarded private coordinates
are outside the response class. The reference, gate, initial sign-box preparation, and boundary
restrictions are all supplied assumptions. The dynamics select changing source preferences and a
persistent grouping within them, but do not discover the erasing architecture.

9.5 Status against the formation standard

Take as selector the map that assigns to each agent the source of smallest reciprocal row cost
eq. (9.8) at the current state, and as handoff the closure time  . The admitted class is open in the
invariant family eq. (9.1), so (F1) holds in its invariant-family form. Selection with a persistence
criterion, (F2), holds: the box pairs are an invariant block relation after  , and  is a function of the
state. Inheritance, (F3), holds for the declared public response class through proposition 9.4, with
the qualification that the parent state is an empirical measure rather than a law pair. Compression,
(F4), fails: the retention is non-injective only on private and gate coordinates that no admitted probe
reads, and it keeps every public child state. Recursion, (F6), fails, since there is a single stage and
the two final boxes stay separated.

For the null-flow control of definition 6.30, delete every peer cost. The public coordinates then follow
the single-agent flows, which keep the two sign boxes invariant by eq. (9.15); the private means
relax monotonically toward zero without changing sign; and the gate means follow eq. (9.14) with
the factor two replaced by one, so the gates still close. The same selector, evaluated along this flow,
therefore reads the crossed pairs while the private advantage dominates and the box pairs after it
is erased. The sequence of selected pairings coincides with that of the reciprocal flow, and only the
switching time changes; the null gates relax at about half the speed. Clause (F5) is therefore met
only through a shift of an event time, and its strong form fails: the final pairing is the sign pattern of
the initial public states and the initial pairing is the sign pattern of the initial private states, and the
null flow preserves both. The construction is a single-stage selection with exact inheritance by a
decoupled-factor projection, not a two-stage selection and not a recursive formation.

Chapter 10

Public compression and inherited
responses

This chapter concerns the reciprocal law potential of definition 4.2, in its exact Gibbs-reduced form
eq. (4.6), with identity channels; it makes no claim about the per-agent or global free-energy pictures.
A nonlinear projection of the reciprocal Fisher flow can discard continuous public differences without
an erasure channel or finite-time equality. The projection is the asymptotic phase of the approach to
a stable common reference, so it compresses the decaying part of the transient. This autonomous
parent nevertheless fails to predict ordinary child sampling, and it is the only parent of its kind. A
separate identifiability result explains why an unrestricted Gibbs interface retains every exposed
child law, and how a fixed channel changes what it retains. The block is supplied and nothing is
selected, so these are retention results rather than formation results; section 10.5 records their
status against the formation standard definition 6.31.

The parent is a virtual collective state, generally different from either the arithmetic or the geometric
pool [1, 63]. The restricted potential N DKL(qc  scR) and metric N gFisher give eq. (10.5). Fine
states remain unchanged by the construction. They approach the common reference, so the
theorem supplies neither persistent nonzero separation nor selected membership, and every fiber
with its parent converges to one point.

The map  is the asymptotic phase of the stable common reference relative to its invariant diagonal:
it is the projection along the strong-stable foliation of the diagonal, whose existence is governed by
the rate condition eq. (10.10) [55]. For periodic orbits this is the asymptotic phase of Guckenheimer
[69], and for a stable equilibrium with a spectral gap its level sets are isostables [106]. The general
theorems are stated for compact normally attracting invariant manifolds in finite dimensions [53]
or for compact invariant manifolds of semiflows on Banach spaces [11]; the diagonal here is a
noncompact subset of a Banach space, so the proof above is given directly in the chart rather than
imported. The construction is an exact dynamical lumping [79]. What the reciprocal interaction
contributes is the spectral gap: the difference rate exceeds the common rate by N = 2N/(N - 1),
which comes from the receiver and sender roles of the peer costs and does not depend on the
temperatures at linear order, because row variations vanish at equality.

that the second order is attained.

10.3 What unrestricted Gibbs probes retain

Consider a block of exposed belief laws qj = fj against a probability reference , with fj bounded
above and away from zero. Fix positive source weights wj and a temperature T > 0. An identity-

of distinct laws gives an invertible Vandermonde system. Every cj vanishes. Its positive factor
e log fjd/T leaves exactly equality of the total weights on each density.

The proof uses a single probe line r = 1 + th, with h outside a finite union of hyperplanes fixed
by the children. Any receiver family that contains such a line therefore identifies the children, and
a restricted family fails only on children whose centered log-density differences are annihilated
by every probe direction. The Vandermonde nodes vj/T approach one another as the children
approach one another, so near the diagonal of theorem 10.1 the resolving power of the probe
decays with the child differences.

In particular, a single ordinary law with one positive weight reproduces all these responses only if
every exposed child law already equals it. The proposition concerns identity comparison channels
and unrestricted receiver probes. It is not an impossibility result for arbitrary channels, restricted
interfaces, or isolated dynamical factors such as theorem 10.1. For a fixed channel its scope is
exactly the following.

possible precisely on the fibers of q  qK restricted to the exposed laws.

Proof. The normalizer depends on the collection only through the weighted channelled densities;
apply proposition 10.3 to them.

For a deterministic coarse-graining channel, the pushforward by a measurable map c, the incoming

gives j = (r - j), closed on the image. For a nondeterministic kernel two sources with equal
channelled laws generally have different channelled velocities, so even the incoming force does
not descend. The within-fiber conditional laws of a deterministic channel are hidden conditionals
of the type treated in chapter 8; whether a deterministic comparison channel combined with that
mechanism yields an exact parent for the full channelled Gibbs interface is not established here.

10.4 The remaining recursive requirement

The phase construction retains one supplied block. A recursive use of any retention needs two
further properties, which we state as a definition.

Definition 10.5 (Controlled projectability and descent of joining). Let a block I have fine state

space XI and a unique flow generated by a vector field VI (xI ; e) that depends on the state e of the

agents outside I in a space Xext. A retention RI : XI  YI , together with an external retention
Rext : Xext  Yext, is controlled projectable if there is a vector field V¯I (y; e¯) on YI , parametrized by

e¯  Yext, with

                   DRI (xI )VI (xI ; e) = V¯I (RI xI ; Rexte),  (10.25)

for all xI and e, and if every declared boundary kernel of the block, including the memory of a reused

child, factors through RI . Within a family of blocks closed under joining, let JI,J : XI × XJ  XIJ
identify the fine state of a union of disjoint blocks. Joining descends if there is a map J¯I,J :

YI × YJ  YIJ with

                   RIJ  JI,J = J¯I,J  (RI × RJ ).               (10.26)

Condition eq. (10.25) is the relatedness of control systems under a surjection, used in hierarchical
control [118], with the external state as the control; for an empty exterior it is the intertwining identity
of eq. (10.8). Condition eq. (10.26) says that the parent of a union is computed from the parents
of its parts, which is what clause (F6) of definition 6.31 needs from a second stage that starts
from first-stage parents. For the phase projection the block is the whole population, so only the
intertwining case has been verified; for proper sub-blocks, where the external state enters VI ,
neither condition has been checked, and the sampling response of section 10.2 already fails to
factor through .

10.5 Status against the formation standard

The phase projection is a retention of a supplied block, the whole population, and the dynamics
selects nothing, so clauses (F2), (F5), and (F6) of definition 6.31 are not addressed. The retention is
non-injective, and an admitted child-level probe, uniform child sampling, distinguishes configurations
in one fiber; but that probe is not inherited by the parent, so (F3) fails for it, and if the probe class
is reduced to responses computed from the phase law, (F4) fails instead. The null-flow control of
definition 6.30 shows where the reciprocal interaction enters. With every peer cost deleted, each
agent follows the diagonal field eq. (10.5) independently, the linearized difference and common
modes then have the same spectrum A, and the rate condition eq. (10.10) fails, since the difference
rate 1 - |J| is smaller than L. The spectral gap N that makes the phase a compression of

                                                113
10. Public compression and inherited responses       MAgent Theory 2.0

differences is therefore produced by the peer costs, but no grouping is selected, and the results of
this chapter are retention and identifiability statements rather than formation.

Chapter 11

Boundary Closure and Recursive
Composition

This chapter concerns the reciprocal law potential of definition 4.2 and its Fisher flow, with identity
peer channels, all-source uniform priors, and a coupled evaluator. It supplies a binary hierarchy
together with an invariant family of agent laws, and proves that the family carries an exact hierarchy
of public compressions. Each level preserves fresh uniform-descendant responses, their subse-
quent evolution, and a declared class of record assimilations. The chapter makes no selection
claim. Membership and the hierarchy are supplied, so clauses (F2) and (F5) of definition 6.31 are
not addressed, and the null flow of definition 6.30 has no selected membership history to reproduce.
The mechanism is an equivariant symmetry reduction (section 11.3). The public partition data that
the hierarchy discards are invisible to the fine energy, the Fisher metric, and the admitted records,
and near the partition-independent laws their contrast decays exponentially under the same flow
(proposition 11.12).

11.1 A general-law family on a supplied tree

Let A and B be probability references on standard Borel spaces with coordinates r and w. Choose
a positive joint density (r, w) against A  B, normalized to one, with bounded logarithm. Its
disintegration supplies a proper model reference and normalized evaluator as in eq. (4.1). It may
couple its arguments; for example, balanced signs (r), (w) give  = exp(J)/ cosh J.

Fix a binary tree of depth d  1 with N = 2d leaves. Each leaf is a primitive agent. For every
internal tree node v, append to the belief sample space an independent public coordinate v with
law v, and append a separate set of such coordinates to the model sample space. The references
extend by these product laws. Each node carries a measurable sign v(r, v)  {-1, 1}. The exact
statements of sections 11.2 to 11.4 use only one property of these signs: conditional on the base,
they are independent and fair. Two realizations are used. In the coin realization, v is uniform
on {-1, 1} and v(r, v) = vsv(r) with a measurable orientation sv(r)  {-1, 1}. In the circle
realization, v is Haar measure on a circle, and a measurable phase function v(r) defines

v(r, v) = sign cos(v - v(r)).                 (11.1)

The sign on its null zero set is immaterial. The atomless circle realization is needed only where
a continuum of balanced partitions is used, namely for the continuous phase families and the
total-variation and Hellinger statements of section 11.5. In both realizations the coordinates v are
original public sample coordinates. Different phase functions or orientations change the laws in
those same coordinates; they are held fixed along a trajectory.

11.3 The hierarchy as an equivariant symmetry reduction

The inheritance statements below are instances of classical facts about equivariant gradient flows.
Let S be the group of pairs  = (, ) in which  = (q, s) consists of fibered bimeasurable maps
of the belief and model sample spaces, q(r, ) = (r, r()) and similarly for s, that preserve
the references, and  is a permutation of the agents that preserves the edge set, the priors, and
the evaluators. The group acts on configurations by ( · q)i = q(i)  q, ( · s)i = s(i)  s, and
( · )ij = (i)(j), with the same rule for model rows.

Lemma 11.4 (Equivariant reduction). In the setting of lemma 11.1, every   S acts on the chart
by a linear isometry of the sup norm, preserves E and the Fisher metric, and commutes with the
flow: if x(t) solves the flow from x0, then  · x(t) solves it from  · x0. Consequently the following
hold. (i) For every subgroup H  S, the fixed-point set Fix(H) is invariant under the flow, and
on it the flow is the Fisher gradient flow of the restriction of E for the restricted metric. (ii) Every
  S maps Fix(H) onto Fix(H-1) and conjugates the restricted flows. A subgroup K  S that
maps Fix(H) into itself, for example a subgroup of the normalizer of H, acts on Fix(H) commuting
with the flow, and the flow descends to the orbit space Fix(H)/K. (iii) A response kernel Q from
configurations to laws on an output space with Q( · x) = Q(x) for   K descends to Fix(H)/K.
If an assimilation map Ao of definition 4.24 satisfies Ao( · x) =  · Ao(x) for   K, and the law of
its record is K-invariant, then every finite adaptive history law of the record-interrupted dynamics
descends as well.

Proof. A reference-preserving bimeasurable q preserves relative entropy, so DKL(q(i)  qq(j) 
q) = DKL(q(i)q(j)), and  preserves the edge set and priors, so the reindexed peer sums
agree. The entropy part of each local term is preserved, and because q is fibered and reference-
preserving, q  q has the same base marginal as q. The evaluator term reads only base marginals,
and  preserves the evaluators, so E( · x) = E(x). The metric is preserved since (q  q)2/(q 
q) = (q)2/q. On log densities the action is i  (i)  q, a linear isometry of L. Direct
substitution in eq. (11.6), including the incoming term, gives hiq( · x) = hq (i)(x)  q, so the field
is equivariant, and uniqueness in lemma 11.1 gives the commutation. For (i), if x0  Fix(H) and
  H, then  · x(t) is a solution from x0 and equals x(t). At a point of Fix(H) the field is H-fixed,
hence tangent to Fix(H), and its metric pairing with every tangent vector v of Fix(H) equals the
derivative of the restricted energy along v; it is therefore the restricted gradient. Statement (ii)
follows from  · Fix(H) = Fix(H-1) and the commutation: if y0 =  · x0 with   K, then
y(t) =  · x(t), so orbits are carried to orbits. For (iii), Q(y(t)) = Q(x(t)), and an equivariant
assimilation keeps related states related while assigning the same law to the record. Induction over
the record times, with the flow between them, gives the history statement.

Statement (i) is the flow form of the principle of symmetric criticality [117], and the invariance of
fixed-point subspaces of equivariant vector fields is standard in equivariant bifurcation theory and
dynamics [56, 67]. The lemma adds nothing beyond these classical facts; it fixes the form in which
they are used here. The following proposition identifies the profile family as a fixed-point set.

Proposition 11.5 (The profile family is a fixed-point set). Fix a realization of the signs. Let
H  S consist of the pairs (, ) such that  is an automorphism of the rooted binary tree acting
on the leaves, and u((i), q()) = u(i, ) for every leaf i and almost every belief sample point ,

each invariant qi is almost everywhere a function Fi(r, ) of the base and the node signs.

Two further subgroups give the quotient. For a measurable map r   (r) into the automorphisms

quotient by these maps, which is the unordered profile tree of section 11.4.

The data discarded by this quotient, namely the phases or orientations and the base-dependent
ordering of branches, are orbit data of a group of exact symmetries of the fine energy and the
Fisher metric. Relative to the observable algebra generated by the fine energy and metric, the fresh
uniform-descendant responses, and the admitted base-only broadcast records, they are gauge: no
agent, channel, record, or energy term of this construction reads them. They are resolved only by
the protocols excluded in section 11.4, namely reused children, shared labels, and child-specific or
unrestricted identity-channel probes. Symmetry does not supply the explicit class costs Dk or their
pair-law form, the incoming term of eq. (11.12), the identification eq. (11.18) of a fresh response
with a subtree mean, the contrast decay of proposition 11.12, or the observability obstruction of
section 11.6; these are computed directly.

The root-level statement holds for every identity-channel configuration, not only on the profile family.

Applying t pointwise to the second configuration gives a path whose spectra are the push-forwards
of the common initial spectra, hence equal to those of x(t). Its scalar inputs therefore coincide

configuration. The rows read only the costs, which agree. A base-only response or likelihood reads
only (r, µq) and multiplies the value vector at r by a common factor, which acts on the spectra.

On the profile family, the conditional law of the value vector given r is uniform on the orbit of the
labeled vector (f (r, u(i)))i under the tree automorphisms, so µq and the unordered profile tree
determine each other. The root case of theorem 11.9 is therefore an instance of proposition 11.6.
What the hierarchy adds is that responses at intermediate nodes, which read physical subtree
membership, also descend; there the relevant descriptors are the conditional spectra of subtrees
given ancestor coordinates. This is the identity-channel analogue of the conditional spectrum of
chapter 8.

are invariant under the fine flow, and when the flow preserves the conjugacy condition, is not

Remark 11.8 (Other symmetric hierarchies). The proofs use only a group of agent permutations
preserving the edges, priors, and evaluator that acts transitively on each set of sibling subtrees,
together with public coordinates that realize at each node a uniformly random arrangement of its
children, fair given the base and ancestor coordinates. Rooted trees with larger branching, realized
by uniform random child permutations, class-constant priors with an edge set that is a union of
common-prefix classes, and phases that depend measurably on ancestor coordinates fall under
lemma 11.4 in the same way. The operator Pk is then replaced by the average that keeps the first k

digits, replaces digit k + 1 by a uniformly chosen different digit, and averages the rest. We do not
write out these cases.

11.4 Recursive retention and the response process

At each base point, arrange the values of f (r, u) in their binary profile tree. Retain this tree with
unordered children at every internal node. Its leaves still carry density values, and its nested
grouping is retained. Flattening it into a multiset would lose which values share a prefix and could
change Dk.

For a physical subtree rooted at depth l, apply this retention only to its descendant values, keeping
the dependence on the base and physical ancestor coordinates. This defines its parent descriptor.
Include the corresponding model descriptor, the shared row-class data, primitive counts, and the
remaining tree connections. At a lowest pair, the unordered values p+, p- can equivalently be
written as a mean (p+ + p-)/2 and a squared contrast ((p+ - p-)/(p+ + p-))2. A first parent
therefore retains more than its mixture law, but does not retain the two full child laws on their original
node coordinates.

Theorem 11.9 (Recursive boundary inheritance on the supplied hierarchy). Under the hy-
potheses of theorem 11.2, these parent descriptors inherit the joint controlled dynamics at every
level of the same fine system. Joining two sibling descriptors gives their unordered pair. The join
commutes with evolution and with fresh uniform-descendant response kernels. Record likelihoods
that depend only on the base and are applied to every agent, used as the assimilation events of
definition 4.24, preserve these statements under arbitrary finite adaptive sequences, whenever the
updates remain in the regular domain.

Proof. By proposition 11.5, the family is Fix(H), and the maps ( , id) and the phase rotations
of section 11.3 act on it as stated there. At a fixed physical point, changing an internal sign
exchanges the two branches below that node. Thus the map from physical leaf labels to their
bit strings is an automorphism of the rooted binary tree. Forgetting its realization removes the
phase at the joined node and leaves exactly the unordered profile subtree. As a direct check
of lemma 11.4(ii), tree automorphisms preserve common-prefix length, Ud, and every Pk. They
consequently preserve eqs. (11.8) and (11.9) and commute with eqs. (11.12) and (11.13), also
when they depend measurably on the base, since the equations have no derivatives in the base
coordinate, the local evaluator reads only f0, g0, and the global integrals are unchanged. The
quotient flow is therefore independent of the chosen ordered representatives.
The quotient admits Borel representatives. Order R2m lexicographically. At each internal node,
from the lowest level upward, place first the child subtree whose current vector of values is
lexicographically smaller. Each step is a finite composition of Borel comparisons and coordinate
permutations, and applying it at each base point to the measurable map r  f (r, ·) gives a
measurable canonical profile that depends only on the unordered tree. This also establishes
measurability of the descended updates.

For partial retentions, the same argument applies to the product of automorphism groups of the
retained subtrees. The complement supplies the retained sibling and ancestor data needed for their
interactions; the joint parent network closes. Thus this is controlled closure for complements in the

                                                              123
11. Boundary Closure and Recursive Composition                            MAgent Theory 2.0

stated prepared family, rather than autonomy under every external law. Combining sibling trees
and then forgetting their ordering is the same operation as retaining their union directly. Repeated
compatible joins give the same descriptor, and joins of disjoint subtrees commute. These are
representation changes inside one fixed N -agent interaction graph. They do not add or delete fine
edges, and do not authorize an arbitrary reassociation of the leaves into another hierarchy.

For a response at a node of depth l, choose a descendant freshly and uniformly, draw its full original
public sample, and conceal its label. At every physical sample point the descendant labels run
through every suffix bit string. The response density is exactly

fl(r, u1, . . . , ul) = Eul+1,...,ud f (r, u1, . . . , ud).               (11.18)

It is the mean of the retained subtree values, with all unused node factors left in the original output
space, and it is invariant under the automorphisms acting below the node, as lemma 11.4(iii)
requires. At the root it is f0(r). Choosing a sibling parent uniformly and then a descendant uniformly
gives exactly the same full sample law. The model sector follows the same rule with a separate
fresh label.

Fix a normalized positive record kernel Lqe(do | r) with bounded positive density on the admitted
update domain, applied as a readout to the original samples of every agent. Every child has base
marginal f0A, so a common record has the same component normalization

unchanged at the record update. Equality of retained states gives equality of the next response law
and the retained update. Induction, using the inherited continuous flow between records, proves
equality of every finite history law under policies choosing the next admitted experiment from the
observed history. At a representation join, the already observed history is carried forward as
controller state; no past record is erased.

The records enter as assimilation events in the sense of definition 4.24. The potential is unchanged
by them, and after an update the force eq. (11.12) depends on the record only through the updated
profile. The admitted records are those whose likelihoods are invariant under the compression
group and that are applied to every agent, which here means base-only and broadcast likelihoods;

public coordinate, for example L(o | r, 0) at the root node, multiplies the profiles of the two root

asymmetry. Records reading ancestor path bits would require retaining the ancestor phases and

Open problem 11.11 (Minimality of the unordered profile tree). Decide whether the unordered
profile tree is minimal for the fresh-response interface of the hierarchy: whether the response
histories of all nodes, under admitted adaptive record policies, separate the base-dependent
tree-automorphism orbits of profiles, at least generically. Proposition 11.13 proves local injectivity
for a different two-agent binary model; for d = 1 and a two-point base, the analogous Jacobian
computation for the root response and its time derivatives is a natural first case.

Each phase can be an arbitrary measurable function of the base. The quotient therefore discards
spatial patterns in the original public laws, beyond a permutation of primitive agents. It retains the
amplitude profile tree, whose size can grow with the number of descendants; no fixed-size parent
representation is asserted.

The sample-coordinate density is piecewise constant in the node coordinates, while the law-valued
Fisher evolution remains smooth in time on the regular profile domain. The result does not give
a smooth dimension reduction on an open law chart. It gives exact recursive public compression
on a prepared invariant class, and that compression is a symmetry reduction. The general base
laws and the coupled evaluator enter only through the base marginals f0, g0, which every level
retains; the compressed data are orthogonal to them. The tree and the class are supplied, and no
endogenous formation time has been derived.

The mechanism relies on complementary child laws whose equal mixture is flat in the public

coordinate. Equal mixtures of Gaussian children do not have this property: with d the standard

normal  density,  1  [d(y  -  v)  + d(y  +  v)]  =  d(y)e-|v|2/2 cosh(y  ·  v)  depends  on  the  direction  of  v

unless v = 0. A continuous phase of the kind used here therefore has no analogue for Gaussian

child laws with a common isotropic covariance.

The reference coordinates r, w in this construction belong to represented sample spaces. They are
not identified with the contextual base C. Applying chapter 3 would additionally require an admitted
smooth context-parameterized family and compatible connections. The measurable retention
proved here does not supply the collective-connection condition in proposition 3.17.

11.6 Why ordinary response completion can remove all compression

The preceding restrictions cannot generally be removed by adding a few response moments to the
phase parent. Observation derivatives can already recover a whole fine configuration, as in the
local observability method of Hermann and Krener [75]. The following calculation uses only the
inverse function theorem.

the reciprocal potential with identity peer channels, binary state and model spaces, the uniform

this includes the range |J| < 1/4 used in chapter 10. There is an open heterogeneous region where
any retention preserving both fresh belief/model mixture responses and their future evolution is
locally injective.

Chapter 12

Two-Stage Selection with Exact
Inheritance on a Wishart Family

This chapter studies the reciprocal law potential of definition 4.2, with its exact Gibbs rows (propo-
sition 4.3) and unit-Fisher dynamics, on an invariant family of matrix Wishart laws. It does not
concern the global or per-agent free energies of chapter 4, and its conclusions are not transferred
to them. Four initially singleton agents are grouped into two parents and then into their union by
a declared threshold rule applied to their evolving laws. Every parent inherits the original-time
dynamics, a declared joint response interface, and the collective connection and contextual tensor
of its children. Every join discards a continuous distinction between model laws.
Measured against the formation standard definition 6.31, the construction is a two-stage selection
with exact inheritance, not a recursive formation. The selector reads belief shapes, and the shape
law  i = -2(i - 0) contains neither the coupling, nor the precisions, nor the model sector, nor
any other agent. Proposition 12.7 shows that the membership history is the count-weighted centroid
dendrogram of the initial belief shapes, read on a clock whose origin is set by the threshold, and that
the null flow of definition 6.30 reproduces it on the entire admitted class. Interaction necessity (F5)
therefore fails, in its strong form as well. Proposition 12.3 identifies the structural cause, which every
architecture with receiver-independent targets and additive moment channels shares. The discarded
model-shape allocation is dynamically inert, and the inherited contextual geometry is prepared in
the initial section, is present at zero coupling, and decays exponentially (proposition 12.11). What
the construction establishes is exact inheritance: original-time parent dynamics with the complete
channel derivative, extensive response histories under adaptive protocols, and preservation of the
collective connection and contextual tensor through both joins.
The architecture is declared. Children have matrix Wishart laws with common precision in each
sector, product recognition, a constant model-independent evaluator, and comparison channels
depending on the population moment. Individual shapes are constant over the contextual base.
Responses use fresh independent samples and return extensive sums. Membership is selected by
a declared threshold rather than by a threshold derived from the potential. The preparation class is
open within this invariant family. Each additive quotient is available initially, and inheritance holds
for every partition at every time, so inheritance does not distinguish the selected partition; the rule
selects when a quotient becomes the operative description. No law is reset at a join.

12.1 Matrix laws and the declared architecture

Let both represented spaces be the cone S2++ of real symmetric positive-definite two-by-two

These primitive self channels are nonidentity channels by constitutive choice. With identity self

reason, promoting the source priors to state variables of the same potential would leave them fixed.

The two sectors have separate population coupling. The evaluator is constant in its model input, and
this assumption is load-bearing. By eq. (4.2), a model-dependent evaluator Gi(m, ·) = W2(0, (m))
would add the term tr(Esi[(m)]X) to the belief force. Because the model laws differ across agents,
the precisions would then cease to be common, and lemma 12.1 would no longer apply to the
parents. The sum-pushforward of independent child evaluator outputs is a kernel from the retained
model sum only because the evaluator ignores the model sample; for unequal precisions (mi)
the sum is not even a Wishart law. With the constant evaluator the belief and model sectors are
uncoupled, and each sector is coupled across agents only through its own population moment.
Outside the Wishart family the displayed functional requires finite relative entropies and moments;
the differential also requires integrable log densities and log determinants, and differentiation under
the integrals along the admitted paths.

12.3 A common relaxation clock

The independence of the shape law from the interaction is an instance of a general identity for
receiver-independent targets.

Proposition 12.3 (Shared targets impose a common relaxation clock). Consider the reciprocal

potential for agents with common state and model spaces. Suppose every agent has the same

model reference r, the same evaluator G(m, dk) = g(dk), constant in m, and that every belief

independent sufficient statistic, then i(t) - j(t) = e-2t(i(0) - j(0)).

proves the second statement. In an exponential family, log(qi/qj) = i - j, S - (i) + (j), and

affine independence of S identifies the coefficients.

For the Wishart family the natural parameter is ( - 3/2, -P), so proposition 12.3 contains both
the shape law and eq. (12.10). Any relabeling-equivariant selector that reads only centered log-
likelihood ratios between agents, for example natural-parameter differences, sees a rescaled copy
of the initial data on a clock shared by every interaction in this class. Interaction-sensitive selection
under the reciprocal potential therefore needs targets that depend on the receiver, for instance
Gibbs rows that are not constant. Whether exact sum closure on an open fiber of child allocations
is compatible with receiver-selective rows is not settled here.

A second obstruction concerns exact additive closure itself.

Adding two parents preserves total moments, counts, and forcing. Shape equations add, and
sample addition gives the joined law and normalized channel. Associativity follows from addition of
the three retained scalars and of the sample matrices.

The theorem holds for every partition at every time, so exact inheritance does not single out the
partitions that the selector of the next section produces; selection and inheritance are logically
independent here. The final single parent still has its inherited nonidentity internal-source channel.
Replacing it by an identity self-comparison would delete the second KL term and change its flow.
A parent source label is the pushforward of one primitive source-label draw; a batch exposing
separate primitive labels would require their joint mark law. Those labels are not exposed by the
interface below.

Exact evolution does not assert equality of fine and parent energies. For example, at P = I2 replace
two shapes 0, 0 by 0 + , 0 - . The total moment and parent state are unchanged, but the
fine energy increases by 2DKL(W2(0 + , I2)W2(0, I2)) + 2DKL(W2(0 - , I2)W2(0, I2)) > 0.
The vector-field calculation, rather than energy factorization, proves inheritance.

12.5 Selected membership

Definition 12.6 (Threshold membership rule). Fix a threshold  > 0 and begin with singletons
whose initial belief shapes are pairwise farther than  apart. For a current block read its mean

                  bI = AI /nI - 0,  bI = -2bI ,  bI J               =  nI bI  + nJ bJ  .  (12.17)

threshold edges join their connected components. Recompute distances after each event.

This rule reads only retained laws and counts, is invariant under relabeling, and contains no supplied
membership tree. The threshold specifies a persistence criterion; it is additional constitutive data.
The separation hypothesis belongs to the domain of the rule: two shapes initially closer than  never
reach  from above and are never joined to each other, even when they are nearest neighbors.
Because every score is explicit, the event times below are computed in closed form, and no
discretization or event-location scheme is involved.

Centroid clustering is one of the pair-group strategies of numerical taxonomy [135], unified with the
other agglomerative strategies by Lance and Williams [90]. In one dimension it has no reversals,
which is the monotonicity in (ii). The rule is not single-linkage clustering. For initial deviations
0, 1, 2.05, 3.5, single linkage joins the third point to the first pair before the last point, whereas the
rule forms the two pairs first, at heights 1 and 1.45, and their union at 2.275. The union time in
eq. (12.20) below already carries the centroid distance d2 +(d1 +d3)/2 rather than the single-linkage
distance d2. The construction also differs from bounded-confidence dynamics [74], in which the
interaction determines which agents cluster. What it adds to centroid clustering is exact inheritance
of laws, dynamics, responses, and geometry at each join.

The persistence statement is part of proposition 12.7; it follows from the equations rather than
from storing a membership flag. Primitive shape differences never vanish at finite time. The two

For loss at a first join, fix all belief shapes and perturb two initial model shapes in that pair by
(i, j)  (i + , j - ) for sufficiently small . The parent model sum, both population moments, all
subsequent precision evolution, and every membership event and time are unchanged. Individual
model laws change continuously. Distinct fixed belief shapes distinguish the labels, so this change
is not a permutation. At the second join, transfer model shape between the two first-parent sums
while keeping their union sum fixed. This gives a further continuous lost distinction and still leaves
the belief-only selection schedule unchanged.

The discarded allocation is a dynamical spectator in both descriptions. Individual model shapes
obey i = -2(i - 0), the model precision depends on the model shapes only through their total,
the belief sector never reads the model laws because the evaluator is constant, and the selector
reads only belief shapes. The witness therefore establishes noninjectivity of the retention, not loss
of a coordinate to which any agent, channel, or selector responds. The belief allocation that the
selector reads is not lost given the event record: at a join the two child scores differ by exactly ,
so the parent sum, the child counts, the join time, , and 0 determine the child belief shapes up
to exchange. The loss witness accordingly uses the model-shape allocation. Already observed
sample records remain with the controller; they are not erased or asserted to have the same law
across different initial preparations. Loss concerns the current parent state and the future interface
specified next.

The hierarchy is transient. All shapes converge to 0, 0, and every precision eigenvalue converges
to the unique positive zero of f (·, 0) or of its model analog, so every agent tends to one common
law. The children are distinct at every finite time, and the consensus is asymptotic rather than
reached in finite time.

The preparation class is nonempty and relatively open. For example take 0 = 0 =  =

and  2  log(17/2).   The  two  first  parents  coexist   for  a  time    2  log(17/6).  A  sufficiently   small      neighbor-

hood and every relabeling obey eq. (12.18). Openness is within the common-precision family, not

among all positive density tuples. The smooth statistical retention applies on each fixed membership

branch; no global smoothness across switching boundaries is required.

Against definition 6.31 the construction meets (F1) for the declared invariant family, open within
it, (F2) with the declared threshold, and (F3) by theorem 12.5, corollary 12.9, and theorem 12.10.
It meets (F4) in the sense that each join retention is noninjective and the singleton responses
available before the join distinguish points of its fiber, although the distinguished coordinate is inert.
It fails (F5) by proposition 12.7. In (F6), the parents select their union under the inherited dynamics
without a reset or a new attraction, but because all scores contract on the common clock, the union
also forms from every counterfactual handoff in which two parent scores are farther apart than ;
